My go-to transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, has a major update today, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and a brand new transcription model. Here's everything new.

MacWhisper's Apple Intelligence integration gets even deeper

I've written in the past about how heavily I rely on MacWhisper, especially for my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper is one of the earliest AI transcription tools available for Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it back in 2023, it has continued to be improved with support for new models, services, and workflows.

These features include automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, folder monitoring, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper is being updated to version 15.2, which introduces an improved speaker identification feature powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was just announced a few hours ago.

Which brings me to another major feature in this update: live meeting transcription.

This feature has been high on MacWhisper's public roadmap, and it's now finally here, allowing users to follow along, review, copy, or send a live transcription during a meeting as it's happening.

On the actual transcription model front, MacWhisper 15.2 is adding Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model with support for 22 languages, alongside deeper integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, users running macOS — including those in the EU — can search transcriptions system-wide, open them with Siri, pull their text into Shortcuts, and reference the currently on-screen transcription in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Lastly, MacWhisper 15.2 is adding folders and subfolders for organizing transcriptions and meetings, with support for dragging and dropping existing transcription files into them from the sidebar.
